title: Capacity Lighthouse: Peak Safety Profiles and Headroom Targets
body:
Summary:
This working sheet defines a small set of "safety profiles" (conservative / balanced / lean) we will use to size and operate the public inference endpoints over the next 6 quarters (horizon: 2026Q4 -> 2027Q4). Instead of writing one static headroom target, the Capacity Lighthouse approach assigns a profile per region and customer tier, and ties autoscale/prewarm knobs and fallback policies to that profile. The goal is predictable latency for 99th percentile requests while minimizing stranded GPU capacity and keeping cost per token within target bands.

Primary objectives:
- Produce region-level peak projections (tokens/sec and QPS) for 2027Q4 at p50/p90/p99.
- Translate projections into per-GPU slice headroom targets and pool sizing guidance by safety profile.
- Define operational triggers (queue depth / tail latency / utilization) that map to prewarm and fallback behavior.
- Produce a short action list to run a 72-hour stress verification and update the admission control rules.

Key assumptions (explicit):
- Workload mix: 65% short-chat (avg 32 tokens output), 25% long-generation (avg 320 tokens output), 10% embeddings/rerank (small token counts but high QPS).
- Model families: 40% Llama-variant quantized (L4/FP8-like), 40% curated open models on H100-optimized kernels, 20% customer pinned larger models (A100/H100 80GB).
- Effective tokens/sec observed on hardware are baseline throughput figures derived from the latest perf bench (June 2026) with KV cache reuse enabled. We expect incremental improvements from kernel updates but do not rely on them for headroom planning.
- Billing quotas and burst-credits are handled separately; this sheet focuses on physical capacity planning.

Region-level peak projections (target horizon: 2027Q4) - tokens/sec / (QPS):
- us-west1: p50 2.1M tok/s (QPS ~6.8k), p90 4.8M tok/s (QPS ~15.6k), p99 7.2M tok/s (QPS ~23.5k)
- us-east1: p50 1.6M tok/s (QPS ~5.2k), p90 3.6M tok/s (QPS ~11.7k), p99 5.6M tok/s (QPS ~18.3k)
- eu-west1: p50 1.2M tok/s (QPS ~4.0k), p90 2.8M tok/s (QPS ~9.2k), p99 4.4M tok/s (QPS ~14.3k)
- ap-southeast1: p50 0.7M tok/s (QPS ~2.3k), p90 1.9M tok/s (QPS ~6.2k), p99 3.0M tok/s (QPS ~9.8k)

Safety profiles (how to interpret and operationalize):
- Conservative profile (S1): multipler = 2.5x above p90 sustained projection. Use for: enterprise customers with SLA-backed latency. Objectives: keep 99th token latency within SLO even when regional microbursts occur. Recommended prewarm: warm extra 30% of pool on predicted peak windows; autoscale thresholds: GPU util >55% sustained for 30s triggers spin-up; queue depth >2.5s triggers emergency fallback to smaller model variant.
- Balanced profile (S2): multiplier = 1.8x above p90. Use for: majority of public traffic, growth-safe. Prewarm: warm extra 15%; autoscale threshold: GPU util >65% sustained 45s; queue depth >4s triggers model variant routing.
- Lean profile (S3): multiplier = 1.4x above p90. Use for: low-cost sandbox and burst-tolerant customers. Prewarm: opportunistic (no dedicated prewarm), autoscale threshold: GPU util >75% sustained 60s; queue depth triggers only when 99th latency > target.

Mapping to GPU slices and pool sizing (examples):
- Effective per-GPU tokens/sec numbers (baseline): H100-80GB: 420k tok/s (mixed workload, KV reuse); A100-40GB: 210k tok/s; L4-type inference card: 95k tok/s (optimized quantized models). These values are conservative and include ~10% headroom for kernel variance.
- Example: us-west1 p90 = 4.8M tok/s. Balanced profile sizing: target capacity = 4.8M * 1.8 = 8.64M tok/s. If pool is H100s only -> need ceil(8.64M / 420k) = 21 H100 GPUs. If mixed fleet (60% H100, 40% A100): capacity equivalent = 0.6*21 + 0.4*(21*(420/210)) -> translate to pool sizing matrix in operational tooling (see linked artifact).

Shortburst (15m window) safety: reserve an additional fast-start buffer of GPUs that can be spun from hot-standby within 90s. Rule of thumb: allocate 12% of Balanced profile capacity as hot-standby for each region during product launch windows.

Operational triggers and routing policies (concrete):
- Admission control: if per-route queue depth > 6s for 3 consecutive 10s windows, route new requests to lower-cost model variant and publish a customer-facing latency signal.
- Prewarm job policy: for windows predicted by traffic forecast with >60% probability of p90 exceedance, schedule a prewarm to reach S2 capacity 5 minutes before window.
- Fallback policy: if an autoscale attempt fails to reach desired capacity within 90s, shift 20% of traffic to cross-region compatible pools and degrade to S2/S3 policies depending on customer tier.

Cost sensitivity and utilization targets:
- Operational sweet spot: target steady-state GPU utilization of 60-70% for Balanced profile; Conservative profile will target 50-60% during peak-preserve windows. Lean profile >70% acceptable but expect higher tail latency risk.
- Cost per effective token sensitivity: running H100s with Balanced sizing vs Lean sizing yields ~18–28% difference in monthly cloud spend for the same p90 performance envelope. Use Optimize recommendations to identify which routes to move to quantized L4 inferencing to reduce unit cost.

Risk matrix (top risks and mitigations):
- Sudden cross-region traffic shift (risk): mitigation: have pre-authorized cross-region fallback pools and rate-limited ingress to prevent cascading autoscale.
- Kernel regression (risk): mitigation: maintain a canary fleet with previous kernel; runway for rollback <30m.
- Queue head-of-line blocking for large-gen requests (risk): mitigation: enforce per-request token cap on public routes and isolate long-gen requests into separate queue with dedicated slices.

Validation plan (72-hour stress verification):
- Night 0: synthetic load against us-west1 to validate prewarm and hot-standby spin-up within 90s. Measure tail latencies and token throughput.
- Night 1: mixed workload test across three regions simultaneously at p99 projected levels for 45m sustained windows. Confirm autoscale triggers and fallback routing.
- Night 2: chaos engineering – induce simulated host failures and kernel slowdowns to validate cross-region fallback and canary rollback process.

Action items (owners and ETA):
- Produce per-route model-variant compatibility matrix for cross-region fallbacks — owner: Aisha Patel — due: 2026-09-10.
- Implement S2 prewarm scheduler prototype in staging and wire into forecasting pipeline — owner: Diego Ramos — due: 2026-09-24.
- Run 72-hour stress verification and publish results to Confluence — owner: Marcus Chen — due: 2026-10-08.
- Add shortburst hot-standby automation (kicker: 90s spin-up) to release backlog — owner: Hannah Li — due: 2026-10-15.

Open questions / discussion points:
- How aggressively do we want to apply model-variant degradation for PLG users vs paid tiers? (affects S3 acceptance thresholds)
- Do we want to commit to a global hot-standby pool for small regions, or keep them regional-local?

Appendix (quick lookup numbers):
- Per-GPU effective tok/s baseline: H100-80GB = 420k, A100-40GB = 210k, L4-equivalent = 95k.
- Safety multipliers: S1 2.5x, S2 1.8x, S3 1.4x.
- Shortburst buffer: 12% of S2 capacity per region during launch windows.

Notes: this is an iterative working sheet and intentionally pragmatic rather than academically optimal. The next revision will replace baseline per-GPU numbers with the July kernel rebench results and a small simulation run that includes mixed-model multiplexing effects.
